recorded_by: Satoshi, successor technical lead, under the owner's grant of 2026-09-26 and the coordinator's stand-down of the same day
why_this_file: the coordinator's stand-down requires every termination recorded with its unit, its limit, its attempt and the cost lost, and requires a cgroup-limit kill distinguished from a user-session memory-pressure kill. None of these is converted into a retry with a bigger cap; the retries this round's driver was configured for were stopped and the arms that were not started stay not started
source_of_every_field: systemd's own journal for the user manager (scope Started / Consumed lines) and systemd-oomd's own kill lines; nothing here is inferred from a process exit code alone

mechanisms.CGROUP_MEMORY_MAX: the kernel cgroup out-of-memory killer fired because the job's own cgroup reached its MemoryMax. The journal shows `Failed with result 'oom-kill'` with NO systemd-oomd kill line. The cap contained the kill to the job that asked for it
mechanisms.USER_SESSION_MEMORY_PRESSURE: systemd-oomd killed the scope because PSI memory pressure for the WHOLE user@1000.service exceeded its 50.00% limit for more than 20 s with reclaim activity, and this scope was the top candidate by usage. The job's own cgroup was NOT at its MemoryMax. No per-job cap prevents this: the trigger is the session's aggregate state, which no single job controls
